summary: Feed s124_double to NDR is degraded: 21.1% of TCP sessions are one-way (needs both directions) and microbursts hit 18.14 Gbps on a 10 Gbps tool port (181% capacity). Both cause incomplete session reconstruction and dropped traffic during bursts, creating blind spots for NDR detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering only one direction for 116 of 551 TCP sessions (21.1% > 10% threshold). NDR requires both directions, so this indicates incomplete bidirectional aggregation - likely asymmetric routing where forward and reverse paths use different links and only one link is tapped/aggregated to this tool port, or SPAN/TAP aggregation is misconfigured.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR cannot reassemble TCP sessions or correlate request/response. Results in incomplete flow records, missed C2/lateral movement detections, and failed handshake analysis for 1 in 5 sessions.

recommended_fix.why: NDR needs_both_directions=true. Aggregating both sides of each flow to the same tool port with flow-aware hashing ensures complete bidirectional visibility without splitting sessions.

findings.root_cause: Traffic microburst peaked at 18.14 Gbps in a 1ms interval, 181% of the NDR's 10 Gbps port capacity (threshold 80%). Packet broker has no load-balancing or burst handling for this feed, so aggregate rate exceeds single tool port line rate.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR port will drop packets indiscriminately during bursts. Even with no packet_drops check firing yet, bursts cause random loss, incomplete payloads (NDR needs_full_payload=true), and missed detections exactly when traffic spikes - often during attacks or scans.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute load across 2x10G NDR ports with flow-aware hashing to keep both directions of each session together, keep utilization under 80%, and absorb 18+ Gbps bursts without drops. Alternative is filter to reduce scope, but load_balance preserves full payload NDR needs.
